content.value_statement: Invalid data often escapes a single check and fails later in execution. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code add validation across multiple layers.
actual_capabilities: Maps where invalid data enters, changes, and reaches risky operations.
Suggests validation at entry points, business logic, environment guards, and debug logging.
Uses TypeScript-style examples for directory validation and workspace initialization.
Shows how test-only guards can prevent dangerous operations outside temporary directories.
Explains how to test each validation layer by trying bypass paths.
limitations: Does not provide a full validation library or framework integration.
Requires the user to adapt examples to their codebase and language.
Does not replace threat modeling, code review, or runtime monitoring.
Debug logging guidance must be adjusted to avoid sensitive production logs.

use_cases.title: Harden Project Setup Paths
use_cases.description: Add layered checks so empty or invalid directories cannot reach workspace or git operations.

use_cases.title: Improve Regression Tests
use_cases.description: Design tests that bypass early validation and verify deeper layers still reject bad data.

use_cases.title: Review Validation Coverage
use_cases.description: Trace data flow through a feature and identify missing checks at each system layer.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one bug path
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the defense-in-depth skill to trace this invalid data bug. Identify each layer where validation should happen and list the missing checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Layered Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply layered validation to this feature. Add entry validation, business logic validation, environment guards, and focused debug logging.

prompt_templates.title: Test Bypass Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Verify that deeper layers protect the system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create tests for this validation fix. Include cases that bypass the entry point and confirm deeper layers reject invalid data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Risky Operation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of command or filesystem side effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this risky operation with the defense-in-depth pattern. Map all inputs, trust boundaries, guards, tests, and logging changes needed.

output_examples.input: A workspace setup accepts an empty project directory and later initializes git in the current directory.
output_examples.output: The response identifies four layers: reject empty paths at project creation, validate workspace inputs, block test git operations outside temporary directories, and log path context before initialization.

output_examples.input: A service validates request fields at the controller but background jobs can create the same object directly.
output: The response maps both entry paths and recommends shared business validation.
It adds tests for controller requests and direct job calls.
It suggests targeted debug logs for rejected invalid objects.

best_practices: Trace the full data flow before choosing validation points.
Validate again at every layer that can be reached through another path.
Keep debug logs focused and avoid secrets or unnecessary payloads.
anti_patterns: Relying on one controller check for all future callers.
Adding logs that expose credentials, tokens, or private user data.
Skipping tests that bypass the first validation layer.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps prevent invalid data from reaching deep execution paths by adding validation at multiple system layers.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it only apply to TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. The examples use TypeScript, but the validation pattern applies to most languages and services.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. It does not include scripts that execute external commands.

faq.question: Should every layer use the same validation code?
faq.answer: Shared helpers can reduce duplication, but each layer should still enforce the assumptions it depends on.

faq.question: How should teams handle debug logging?
faq.answer: Log only the context needed to diagnose failures, and remove secrets or sensitive payloads from logs.
